blocks.text: The three men refuse coerced worship while openly accepting that rescue may not come. Their deliverance does not turn the chapter into a single rule for every faithful response under imperial pressure; it portrays endurance and resistance without requiring either compliance, escape, revolt, or an expectation of miraculous rescue. The fourth figure is described in the chapter with divine-being and angelic language. Identifying that figure directly as the preincarnate Christ reflects a later Christian interpretation rather than the chapter’s own explicit identification.

Their words, “But if not,” are central to the scene: they will not worship the image even if they are not spared from the furnace. The story therefore does not promise that every persecuted person will survive, nor does it make those who are not delivered responsible for their suffering.
